# Sarpo (01, engineer) — BAD-063

## Brief
A take that a collab member has already uploaded through a signed URL can be
refused 403 `closed` and lost forever. Fix it, and decide the rule that
replaces the accident.

## The defect, precisely

`loadRoom` (server/supabase/functions/collab/room.ts) is the membership gate
every member-scoped mode runs through, and it WRITES: a room in `wrapping`
with no fresh recording heartbeat is flipped to `wrapped` — in the database
and on the very `collab` object it hands back — before the mode is dispatched
at all. `commitUpload` (collab/push.ts) then runs its own phase gate,
`writablePhase(collab.status)`, which admits `open | live | wrapping` and not
`wrapped`, and answers 403 `{error:'closed',code:'closed'}`. No
`collab_takes` row is ever written, though the member has already spent the
bytes.

Two things make this reachable rather than theoretical:

1. A booth that stops recording sends `heartbeat … recording:false`, which
   clears `recording_at` — so the seat goes COLD in the window between "the
   take finished recording" and "the take's commit landed". That window
   contains an upload of the whole clip.
2. The beat that turns the seat cold is itself judged while the seat is still
   hot, so it is the NEXT request that completes the wrap. That next request
   is very often the member's own `upload-url` or `commit`, or another
   member's 60-second `info` poll.

The consequence the ticket also names: commit's OWN wrap-completion copy
(push.ts, the `if (collab.status === 'wrapping')` block near the end) is
unreachable outside a sub-millisecond race — whenever it would fire, the gate
has already fired. The two copies are deliberate near-duplicates (push.ts's
head comment says so, and BAD-047's spike risk 9 said leave both alone in the
split); one of them is currently dead code.

The whole point of the `wrapping` phase is that whoever is mid-part finishes.
Today it is the phase in which their work is most likely to be destroyed.

## Pinned, as the wrong behaviour

`test/server/functions.test.mjs`, `collab: a wrapping room finishes on the
next member read, and the take after that is refused` (around line 2955 on
main) walks the whole sequence and asserts today's 403 with `collab_takes`
still holding 2 rows. Its comments say outright that it pins "the behaviour
it is, not the behaviour anyone designed", and name BAD-063. That test is
yours to invert: it becomes the regression test for the rule you choose, and
its comments must explain the rule rather than the accident.

## What the fix must be true of

- A take whose bytes the server told the member to upload must land, or the
  member must be refused BEFORE they spend the upload. Losing a recorded take
  silently is the bug; no shape that still loses one is a fix.
- A genuinely abandoned wrap — the last hot seat crashed or scrapped its
  take, so no commit ever arrives — must still reach `wrapped` with no cron,
  and keep the `WRAPPED_TTL_MS` retention rather than being destroyed by the
  idle sweep. That is why the read-side copy exists (design D3); do not
  simply delete it.
- A room that is genuinely finished must not stay open to writes. Whatever
  grace you grant has a bound, and you say what bounds it.
- Both surviving copies of the wrap-completion rule must remain safe under a
  race with `reopen` and with a concurrent commit — today that safety is the
  `where … and status = 'wrapping'` guard on the UPDATE. Keep it, or replace
  it with something you can argue is as strong.

## Shapes to weigh (pick one, with evidence; not a menu to take on faith)

- **Mode-aware read gate.** The read-side wrap stands aside when the request
  it is gating is itself a write the `wrapping` phase admits (a `take`
  `commit`, and probably its `upload-url`), and lets commit's own copy decide
  after the row lands. Simple, and it restores commit's dead copy to service.
  Note its limit before you choose it: it does nothing when ANOTHER member's
  `info` poll wraps the room while your commit is in flight — the database
  already says `wrapped` when your commit arrives, and the loss is identical.
- **Bound the hot window to the round trip.** The seat stops counting as hot
  only once its take has landed (or a bounded time after `recording_at` goes
  stale), so the wrap cannot complete underneath an upload at all. Closest to
  the design's intent; costs a definition of "landed" and a new bound.
- **A bounded grace on commit.** `commit` of a `take` admits a `wrapped` room
  for a short, explicit window after `wrapped_at`. Cheap, but it widens what
  a finished room accepts, so the bound had better be small and argued.

Combinations are allowed. Prefer a SERVER-ONLY fix: if you conclude the only
correct answer needs the web/iOS booth to change (for example, holding
`recording:true` through the upload), do NOT reach into the client — file a
`proposal` for it and take the best server-side fix you can, or
`member block` if no server-side fix is honest on its own.

Do not silently absorb **BAD-038** ("Share the wrap-completion rule between
collab info and commit"), a queued P3. If your fix leaves one copy, or makes
sharing them the obvious next move, say so in your return so that ticket can
be closed or re-aimed deliberately — but do not do BAD-038's refactor as a
side effect of this one.

This is `functions/collab/*.ts` and possibly `_shared/collab.mjs`, so
`.claude/skills/server-changes` sets the bar: a green `npm test` proves
NOTHING here on its own — the integration suite skips without a local stack.
You need `test/server/functions.test.mjs` ACTUALLY RUNNING against a local
Supabase stack, and you must show the output of the collab tests, or say
plainly in your return that you could not get a stack up so the proof has to
be the `Server integration` check on the PR. Containers are podman, never
Docker; `server/README.md` § Local development has the `DOCKER_HOST` and the
`-x edge-runtime,vector,logflare` the start needs. Never `supabase login`, a
`SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, or a `db push`: deploys are CI's.

Run `npm test` too, and say which suites ran.
